title: Operator norm of an n-covector is at most P^n times its Euclidean coefficient norm
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P, i.e. a continuous alternating n-linear map α : (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n). Let ‖α‖ be its operator norm (the norm of continuous alternating maps, ‖α‖ = sup{|α(v_0,…,v_{n−1})| : ‖v_k‖ ≤ 1}) and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i is the standard orthonormal basis. Then ‖α‖ ≤ P^n·|α|.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ‖α‖ ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ n * covectorEuclideanNorm α
